coarse_request: Please design a prototype development process that includes the roles of 'R&D team'. The key activities are 'prototype building' and 'prototype testing', and there should be decision points regarding 'prototype refinement' and 'final prototype approval'.
fine_grained_text:
Step 1: The process starts with identifying an idea for a new product or improvement to an existing one.
The R&D team conducts initial research and feasibility studies, followed by drafting design concepts.
After selecting a promising design, a prototype is built using available materials and resources.
The prototype undergoes various tests to assess its functionality, safety, and market potential.
Feedback from the testing phase is collected, and the prototype may be refined accordingly.
If a refinement is needed, then the testing phase is reinitiated.
The process ends when the prototype is either approved for further development or discarded.



Please design a prototype development process that only includes the roles of 'R&D team'. The key activities are 'prototype building' and 'prototype testing', and there should be decision points regarding 'prototype refinement' and 'final prototype approval'.
[Transition]: The transition from Process A to Process B occurs when the R&D team's final prototype approval triggers the warehouse to begin sourcing parts for production. This process is initiated by a customer order, which prompts the assembly of the newly developed product.
Step 2: An order to cash process starts when a customer order is received.
After the order has been processed, it is sent to the warehouse.
The warehouse employees determine the parts required to produce the requested items.
If any parts are not available in the warehouse, these are ordered.
Once all necessary parts are available, production will start.
After production, quality checks will be performed.
If the production process has finished, products will be packaged and labeled, before returning to the warehouse.
Finally, sales will be informed about the completed production and the product can be sold to the customer.
[Transition]: Once the warehouse is informed of the completed production, the specific properties for the custom chainsaw are defined, triggering the ordering of specialized parts required for Process B.
Step 3: Title: Chainsaw

You produce custom chainsaws on demand.
Your chainsaws have at least 5 properties such as length of the "guide bar" (Schwertlaenge), chain width, electric or motor chainsaw.
After your customer told you the properties, you can start ordering the parts from various online sources (in parallel).
After the parts arrive you have to do a manual inspection of all parts, and then assemble the parts.
During production, you regularly send updates to your customer.
After producing the first saw you send it to your customer.
If he likes it, the rest of his order are produced.
[Transition]: After the first custom chainsaw is assembled and delivered to the customer, the machine is configured to produce the remaining units; OEE tracking begins to monitor the efficiency of this specific production run.
Step 4: Title: OEE

Write a process, that collects relevant information from a machine, and calculated the Overall Equipment Efficiency (OEE).
If the OEE falls below a certain value/percentage, stop the machine and send an email to an engineer.
When the machine is restarted, continue measuring.
When the machine is disconnected, stop the process.
[Transition]: The OEE process halts the machine only when performance drops below the threshold, signaling the need for a hardware modification; this triggers the construction of a new custom machine using Lego bricks.
Step 5: Title: Building a custom machine out of Lego bricks

When building a custom machine out of Lego bricks, you first need to develop the basic design.
After that, you order certain Lego brick sets.
You give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you (into a number of containers).
Your machine is built out of a number of subcomponents.
You build them individually, using parts from the sorted containers.
If there are no more parts in a container, you reorder individual parts.
After building each subcomponent, you have to test them individually and (if each test is successful) assemble them.
If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them.
[Transition]: The successful assembly of the Lego machine provides the physical proof-of-concept needed to initiate formal product development, triggering the R&D team to begin feasibility studies and design drafting for the new product.

If a refinement is needed, then the testing phase is reinitiated.
The process ends when the prototype is either approved for further development or discarded.
[Transition]: The prototype developed in Process A is approved for further development, leading to the production of a luxury airplane in Process B.
Step 7: Title: Luxury Airplane

You produce airplanes.
While the base model is always the same, your customer likes to pimp their airplane with fancy interior.
You let them decide between a number of 5 different bars, the number of seats, their color, and the amount of water in the toilets of their plane (you can come up with additional stuff).
After you received the specifications you send the requirements to different teams to manufacture the parts.
E.g. manufacturing the vodka bar is done by the Russian team, the whiskey bar is manufactured by an Irish team.
After receiving the individual bits and pieces, the interior of the plane is assembled, and the plane is sent on a test flight.
During the flight you create a test protocol which is sent to you and the customer.
The plane is delivered to the customer, which has to confirm.
